People need to understand the difference between freedom of speech, censorship, and moderation.

The government enacts free speech. i.e. they won't arrest you for most things. However, that does have limits (threats on the president's life, bomb threats, yelling fire, libel, etc.)

Anyone can censor by just removing things they don't like.

Organizations are free to moderate discussion as well. They do this by selective censorship of things that derail discussion, or may cause other participants to self censor. i.e. removing insults and slurs to clean up discussion.

What people need to understand is that as long as the government is not moderating and censoring all your speech, it's not an attack on free speech. A university saying "We don't want people calling black students slurs, because we want them to be able to participate in discussion" is moderation, and does not affect your freedom of speech. This is a big difference, and I feel like a lot of people miss this point.

This is a very big point that needs to be said. The key thing being that the first amendment only applies the restriction on the government, meaning private institutions, ie. private colleges, can do whatever they want invloving censorship or moderation so long as it only applies on their property only.

I'm not a fan of it in the slightest, but I'm just bringing up an argument over legality.
